review: vocal-music@1 adds one general operation, vocal-music (learning 2 at 0.2 energy per study round), registered last for long-ex25: mode hum or sing starts a bout of 1-3 rounds at 0.5 energy per voiced round and no material, with a phrase of 2-8 notes (pitch -4..4 steps from a home note 0, 1-4 beats) or improvise=true, and sing may add text within tell's 240-character limit; resume continues a paused bout after fresh checks and cancel ends it at once for no energy. Hearing reuses foundation-expression@1: expressionHearers and expressionHear were factored out of the tell and invite delivery without behavior change (the ex18 replay keeps its exact hashes) and are called, not copied; tell is never invoked. Each voiced round emits one segment at the performer's position, and every other living person within the tell radius (vision, 5) at the end of the round, seen or not, gets a heard event and an entry in the same bounded heard list (6 entries) with kind hum or sing, a sound label, the phrase, the words and the source segment, never a text field, so it reads as sound and can displace older spoken entries. Modeling assumptions: a segment renders the whole phrase once; quiet is a fixed label, with no loudness, tuning, tempo, attenuation or masking; no unconsciousness or vocal impairment is represented, so pain means an injury event in the last or current round and distress means satiety 0 or a body temperature outside 7-34, where forest physiology deals thermal damage; the limits are 3 voiced rounds in any 10 rounds and 2 unvoiced rounds after 3 voiced rounds in a row or in one bout, shared by study, hum and sing in one per-person record, a start must fit every requested round and a resume every remaining one, so after the two study rounds only one more voiced round fits until the window moves; study is the kernel's own and cannot be refused mid-way, so its rounds count as voiced and are heard as hummed practice phrases, except rounds in pain or distress, which still progress but stay silent and unvoiced, and the resumption after an energy pause is the kernel's; improvisation uses FNV-1a of the id and start round seeding xorshift32, never randomness, and study rounds hum the phrase of their own round; another action or a refused round pauses the bout at the end of that round, failed checks on a continuing round pause it without charge, repeating the start never resumes it, death ends the bout and any study with no continuation after respawn, and nothing is refunded; joining has no mechanics of its own, as each person uses their own mastery and hears the others. There is no object, item, process or lasting sound, only the per-person record of the last 10 rounds, rest, study rounds and the last bout, with the open bout shown as active work. There is no reward: no satisfaction rule; the install's practice rule cannot fire because the completion event never carries a qualified flag and nothing material changes; segment events carry no top-level progress fields, so they earn no routine progress credit; incentives are off here, and a check in expression-incentives gated on vocal-music@1 keeps segments and heard music from counting as contact, activity or use, so music never triggers answered, two-way or work-noticed, and voicing beside someone's made thing is not noticing it. Visuals: no components, only view metadata on events, with a voice or hum glyph only on executed segments, neutral paused, cancelled and ended states, completion only after every requested segment, and no badge.
